title: Common projective sheaf charts for two integral constructible complexes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], work on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and use $D(B_W)$, the unbounded derived category of $B_W$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

For every qcqs $S$ appearing below, likewise put $B_S=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_S$. Let $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Choose finitely many finite partitions of $W$ by locally closed constructible subschemes, on whose strata the residue-cohomology sheaves of $M$ and $N$ are locally constant [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. There is a finite rooted binary tree of qcqs locally closed subschemes with root $W$, each internal vertex split into a quasi-compact open subscheme and its closed complement, with the following property. On each nonempty leaf $T$, both restricted complexes are derived complete [def-weil-derived-complete], and their derived residue reductions have only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, all locally constant with finite-dimensional $R/(\varpi)$-vector-space local models [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves, def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Each leaf maps scheme-theoretically through a stratum of every one of these chosen partitions.

For each such $T$ there is an affine pro-etale cover $V\to T$ with $V$ weakly contractible (evaluation on $V$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections), and a finite disjoint open cover $V=\coprod_i U_i$ on which both $M$ and $N$ have bounded $B_{U_i}$-module-sheaf representatives $P_i,Q_i$. Every term of these representatives is a direct summand of a finite sum of $B_{U_i}$: it has an inclusion into $B_{U_i}^{\oplus r}$ and a retraction whose composite is the identity. The opens $U_i$ are qcqs, and the composite maps $U_i\to T$ form a covering. Their differentials may be arbitrary $B_{U_i}$-linear sheaf maps. No Noetherian hypothesis on $W$, and no assertion that these differentials are constant over $R$, is imposed. For $W=\varnothing$ the tree and its empty leaf have no chart conditions.

source.place: Tag 09C3, lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex, using the finite open–closed refinement and residue Tor bound already stated in lem-fix-constructible-open-closed-refinement and lem-fix-constructible-flat-cohomology-tor-bound. Common-chart formulation of returned item steps 3 and 4, with Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 6.5.5 and 6.5.8.

proof.text: Apply the finite residue-lisse tree theorem to the two complexes and the given partitions. For a leaf, instantiate its qcqs weakly etale restriction assertion at the identity to recover the required leaf residue conditions.

Use the single affine weakly contractible ring cover from clause (2) of hypercover existence. The weak-contractibility equivalences give the epimorphism-evaluation property in the covering scheme's own site. Uniqueness of the arrow to the terminal object identifies its displayed singleton cover.
Apply the affine common-projective-chart theorem to the restriction along the covering map composed with the leaf immersion, using the tree's stability on qcqs weakly etale objects.

The singleton pro-etale cover is surjective on points. Lift any leaf point to the affine cover and then to a member of its finite open cover; this proves the stated coverage of the leaf. Associativity identifies each composite model morphism. Empty leaves require no charts.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q88-89333f201 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 13 cited statements, Stacks 09C3 (proetale.tex lemma-local-structure-constructible-complex) and Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.5.8 and Remark 6.5.10. It is a first split (no 2026-10-21 re-split note), the statement is unchanged and there are no new nodes. Steps 1–7 are sound. (1) The open-closed refinement node gives the tree and the morphisms from each leaf to its strata. (2) The locality restriction clause covers both children: the open child is weakly étale and qcqs, and the closed child's complement is quasi-compact. (3) Homology, composition and locally-constant pullback over the finite field k give the residue assertions on each leaf. (4) Hypercover clause (2) gives the cover V, and completeness passes to V. (5) The Tor-bound conclusion is verbatim the Tor hypothesis of the projective-model node. (6) Its derived-limit completeness is the definition in def-weil-derived-complete. (7) Clopen intersections are qcqs, and the clopen coefficient comparison is exact, so quasi-isomorphisms and retractions survive. Edge cases checked: W empty, empty partition list, M or N zero, different intervals and charts, nonreduced strata, non-Noetherian W. No duplicate found: integral-heart-local-model, adic-residue-lisse-perfect-lift and pbc local-effectivity are Noetherian or have stronger conclusions. Repaired two faults. B4: steps 3–7 had TeX corrupted into control characters (\varpi, \to and \beta lost) and missing backslashes on \alpha, \leq, \coprod, \cap and \mathrm; restored. C1/C4: step 4 took 'V weakly contractible for its own site' from det-pe-hypercover-existence, which only gives a w-contractible ring D. It now cites det-pe-weak-contractible-equivalences (Spec D with D w-contractible is weakly contractible, applied with X=W=V); this is added to proof_deps and split_report.tool_uses. Accepted tool uses: the pur homology and composition nodes, exc locally-constant pullback, det-pe-hypercover-existence clause (2) and det-pe-weak-contractible-equivalences.
